blinding_guess.why: All ten packet elements are public members of kobuki::Kobuki in kobuki.hpp, each with a matching definition (inline or in kobuki.cpp), and the getters return the payload structs whose layouts match the length fields the driver checks. The only irregularities seen are internal: DiffDrive leaves last_timestamp and last_diff_time uninitialised, so the first updateOdometry call can return junk pose_update_rates, and the getting-started doc says updateOdometry fuses gyro heading while the code uses encoders only. Neither looks like an interface defect.

notes: Pure C++ driver library (packet ros_generation 'other'; built with catkin). All elements are C++ API symbols, not ROS topics, so msg_type and definition_id are null (no .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition exists for them) and all QoS fields are null. No rate is set for any element; the driver streams at whatever rate the robot sends, with a 0.1 s data-stream watchdog (kobuki.cpp:165) and a 4000 ms serial read block (kobuki.cpp:96), neither of which is declared as a rate for these accessors. Frames: no frame identifier is declared anywhere in kobuki_driver for these accessors; frame is null for the spatial ones (heading, angular velocity, inertia, odometry, cliff PSD, dock IR, core sensors) and 'none' for motor current, general-purpose I/O and init(). Units: getAngularVelocity 'rad/s' rests on the kobuki.cpp:398 comment ('raw data angles are in hundredths of a degree, convert to radians') applied to angle_rate; the per-second part is implied by the field name, not stated. getInertiaData units come from the same comment (kobuki.cpp:391 and 398) applied to the raw fields; acc[3] has no stated unit and the protocol doc (en_appendix_protocol.dox:413-417) marks angle and angle rate only as 'Factory calibrated'. updateOdometry units are left null: they are derivable (wheel_radius and bias in [m], diff_drive.cpp:35-36; tick_to_rad; time_stamp ms / 1000, diff_drive.cpp:92), which gives m/rad for pose_update and m/s, rad/s for pose_update_rates, but no unit is stated for these outputs. Current: the protocol doc lists each motor as 2 bytes but Length 2 (en_appendix_protocol.dox:461-463); the code reads one uint8_t per motor (current.hpp:44), consistent with the Length field. exclusive is empty: init()/spin() open the serial device parameters.device_port (default "/dev/kobuki", parameters.hpp:40) and are the only writers of motor commands through it, but neither the code nor the configuration in the snapshot declares exclusive access (no O_EXCL/TIOCEXCL/lock), and ecl::Serial's behaviour is outside the snapshot. references is empty because the packet lists no consumed elements; the code relies on ecl library APIs (ecl::Serial, ecl::DifferentialDrive::Kinematics, ecl::Angle, ecl::Pose2D), which are not recorded. The getXXX accessors do not lock internally; callers must use lockDataAccess()/unlockDataAccess() (kobuki.hpp:113-114). Firmware major-version mismatch sets shutdown_requested (kobuki.cpp:284-295); that is a stop, not recovery. Other observations: DiffDrive::update uses function-static init_l/init_r (diff_drive.cpp:59-60), shared across instances; GpInput::serialise writes Length 10 while deserialise consumes 7 uint16 values (gp_input.hpp:57, 86-93); the doc length is 16 (en_appendix_protocol.dox:573). The snapshot also contains other kobuki packages; only snapshot/kobuki_driver was used.
